title: Adaptive failover guard for dependency/model/tenant isolation
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: Current breaker behaviour is coarse-grained and mostly reactive: per-tenant breakers and simple per-model rate limits either over-trips (causing unnecessary global fallbacks) or under-trips (allowing degraded calls to escalate costs and latency). We lack a unified strategy that (a) ties breaker decisions to SLOs, (b) differentiates between dependency failures vs model degradation, and (c) supports safe, staged fallbacks across regions and model variants.

Goal: Implement an adaptive failover guard and dependency quarantine layer that: 1) evaluates trip decisions with SLO-aware thresholds, 2) maintains per-entity (dependency/model/tenant) state with isolation windows, and 3) executes a deterministic, observable fallback chain (local cache -> cheaper model variant -> delayed retry -> region failover) with minimal user-visible regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive breaker exposes per-entity (tenant/model/dependency) metrics and states in Console dashboard
Breaker trip decision uses sliding-window SLO mapping and is tunable via Console (error/latency/50/95/99 thresholds)
Graceful fallback chain implemented and exercised in canary: cached response -> quantized model variant -> deprioritized async retry -> region failover
Rollout plan with staged percentages and automatic rollback on regression is implemented
E2E load tests and chaos injections show no increase in customer-facing error rate beyond acceptable SLO budget during simulated dependency outages
design_notes: Core idea: compute a per-entity risk score combining three signals: recent error rate, p95 latency deviation from baseline, and resource contention (GPU queue length / batch saturation). Use a weighted sliding-window exponential decay (default window 5 minutes, decay alpha 0.3). Trip threshold tiers: advisory (risk > 0.35) -> throttling (risk > 0.6) -> quarantine/trip (risk > 0.85).
trip_thresholds: Advisory: risk_score > 0.35 => emit alert and apply soft backpressure (request pacing, reduce batch sizes)
Throttling: risk_score > 0.6 => reduce concurrency for entity, reject non-critical routes, and switch to prefetched cache for cold prompts
Quarantine/Trip: risk_score > 0.85 => short-circuit to fallback chain; open breaker for 30s with progressive cooldown (exponential backoff capped at 10m)
fallback_strategy: Fallback chain (in order): 1) Serve cached/prefetched completion if similarity > 0.85; 2) Route to quantized or distilled model variant pinned to same API contract; 3) Return structured degraded response with explicit 'partial' flag and reason; 4) If still failing and cross-region enabled, perform region failover to next healthy region with per-tenant routing rules; 5) As last resort, return user-friendly error with retry-after header and add to async retry queue for background reconciliation.
multi_region_considerations: Prefer local-region mitigation (quantized model variant, cache, throttling) before cross-region failover. Before initiating region failover check: health of target region, data residency constraints per tenant, and propagation of KV-cache warmup to avoid cache stampede. Region failover uses a staged redirect (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated SLO checks at each stage.
telemetry_and_alerting: Expose new metrics: entity.risk_score, entity.error_rate_1m, entity.latency_p95_ratio, entity.queue_saturation, entity.breaker_state. Add Console charts and alerts: risk_score > 0.5 for 2m, breaker_trips/sec > baseline * 3, and cached_hit_rate drop > 20%. Create synthetic monitors to validate fallback chain correctness.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind runtime-ff for internal org only. 2) Canary: route 5% of traffic from non-sensitive tenants for 48h. 3) Expand to 25% with automated SLO monitors for 24h. 4) Full rollout with 7-day burn-in. Rollback triggers: sustained p99 increase > 2x or error-rate increase > tenant SLO budget.
testing_plan: Unit tests for risk scoring math and deterministic breaker transitions. Integration tests for fallback chain (simulate model errors, high latency, GPU OOM). Load tests: synthetic tenants at 2x traffic for 1h while swapping target dependency. Chaos: network partition and slow downstream responses injected in staging to validate quarantine behavior.
progress_updates: 2026-02-21 - Initial design sketch posted to engineering Slack and RFC document created (link in runbook_refs). Marco: added baseline risk formula and decay constants.
2026-02-28 - Prototype implemented in runtime sandbox by Aisha; basic risk_score computed and exposed via /internal/metrics endpoint. Observed expected sensitivity to injected 5xxs.
2026-03-03 - Design review with PM and Security. Feedback: must include explicit tenant data-residency guard before region failover and ensure KMS keys not leaked during cross-region ops.

2026-03-07 - Load-testing: simulated model droppings (OOM) for 10 minutes on a single node. Breaker quarantined model variant and fallbacks triggered; p99 latency stayed within SLO for canary tenants. Noted secondary effect: cache warmup spike on failover.
2026-03-10 - Incorporated throttling stage and exponential cooldown. Preparing canary feature-flag rollout ticket and runbook updates. Next: coordinate with Platform for region warmup and KMS review.
